title: Microturn flow debugging and SDK replayability - PRD draft
content:
Summary:
This doc sketches a PRD for developer-first features to make short-lived conversational turns (microturns) observable, debuggable, and replayable end-to-end through the Hosted API stack. Focus areas: incremental streaming frames, deterministic tool-call replay, compact structured output checkpoints, and SDK ergonomics for local replay + test harnesses.

Problem statement:
Teams building interactive features hit three pain points: 1) intermittent partial responses (streaming) make root-cause hard to find; 2) tool calls (HTTP/SQL/exec) interleave with generation and are hard to reproduce; 3) structured outputs evolve and regress silently in production. Debugging across client, SDK, and server is manual and time-consuming.

Goals:
- Provide a reproducible microturn capture format that includes partial frames, tool-call events, and final structured output.
- Offer SDK primitives to capture and replay microturns locally with deterministic ordering and optional synthetic tool stubs.
- Add server-side lightweight checkpoints for structured output validation and schema diffs.
- Surface developer-first telemetry and a minimal replay UI for triage.

Non-goals:
- Full deterministic model re-execution (we will not attempt to re-run model RNG to identical tokenization across quantized variants).
- Replacing heavy audit logs or complete session recording at the retention tier.

User stories:
- As a frontend engineer, I want to save a failing microturn and replay it in the dev SDK to reproduce a tool handshake bug.
- As an SRE, I want microturn samples attached to error traces to correlate latency spikes with tool timeouts.
- As a product owner, I want schema diffs for structured outputs when a model rollout changes keys/nesting.

Success metrics:
- Time to reproduce: median developer reproduce time for microturn bug drops from ~2.3h to <30m.
- Bug triage: % of production partial-response incidents with attached replay artifacts > 60% within 24h.
- Adoption: SDK capture-replay used by 30% of active hosted-api customers within 6 months (opt-in).

Constraints and privacy:
- Captures must respect PII redaction rules (configurable client-side mask).
- Capture size budget per microturn: default 128KB compressed.
- Retention: ephemeral by default; opt-in uploads stored for 7 days unless customer explicit export.

Design (high level):
1) Microturn Capture Format (jsonl): incremental frames with monotonic seq ids. Fields: frame_id, seq, partial_text_delta, tokens_meta (optional), tool_event (nullable), client_metadata, timestamp, checksum. Tool_event includes type, request_id, start_ts, end_ts, outcome, stub_hint. Example line: {"frame_id":"f-1","seq":3,"partial_text_delta":"...","tool_event":null,"ts":"2025-02-10T16:12:34Z"}.

2) Deterministic Replay API (SDK):
- SDK.capture.startMicroturn(meta) -> returns microturn_id
- SDK.capture.writeFrame(microturn_id, frame)
- SDK.capture.finish(microturn_id, final_metadata)
- SDK.replay.run(microturn_id, {toolStubProvider}) -> stream events locally, ability to pause/step/inspect frames
Notes: toolStubProvider is a function map used during replay to synthesize tool responses deterministically.

3) Tool-call handshake model:
- Explicit tool_event frames inserted into the capture with call/response envelopes and trace_ids.
- Each tool_event has idempotency_key; replay will surface mismatch warnings if wire-timeouts or ordering differ.

4) Structured-output checkpoints:
- After canonical end-of-turn, capture contains final_structured_output and a compact fingerprint (schema hash + key diff). Server will optionally run quick schema validation and emit a 'schema-diff' artifact that highlights added/removed keys and type changes.

SDK ergonomics and dev flow:
- Minimal surface: three new SDK methods (startMicroturn, writeFrame, replayMicroturn). Default capture is lightweight; opt-in full payload.
- Replay harness: CLI command `ri microturn replay <file>` that spins a local websocket + tool-stub playground to step through frames.
- Local dev mode auto-stubs common tool types (http, sql, exec) by pattern matching request signatures; developers can register deterministic responses.
- Telemetry: capture snippet ids can be attached to api call metadata: X-RI-Capture-ID for server-side lookup in traces.

Streaming protocol considerations:
- Preserve existing incremental streaming channel (SSE/WS). Capture uses only a local SDK buffer until finish/flush.
- For low-bandwidth clients, allow `sampled=true` to only capture error frames.
- Backpressure: SDK will expose a low-memory mode that keeps only keyframes every N frames.

Operational and security notes:
- Captures uploaded to Hosted API are scanned for secrets using existing redaction pipeline before being stored.
- ACLs: capture artifacts inherit customer tenancy and are only accessible via console/owner token.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (4 wks): API + SDK PoC, internal-only, CLI harness, basic replay.
- Phase 1 (8 wks): opt-in public beta for power users; retention 7d; server-side schema differ.
- Phase 2 (ongoing): console integration (microturn viewer), sampled telemetry, templates for common tool stubs.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How to represent anonymized token-level diffs without leaking model internals? (privacy + IP concern).
- Storage sizing: default sample rate and compressed sizes need ops validation.
- UX: should replay UI allow live edits of frames and re-injection into hosted pipeline? (risk of misuse).

Next steps / TODOs:
- TODO @Diego: spike on storage compression and estimated cost for 1000 captures/day (due 2025-02-02).
- TODO @Sofia: prototype CLI replay and web viewer minimal wireframes (due 2025-02-14).
- Create Jira epic RI-3142 and link PRs for SDK changes.

Notes / references:
- See related: RI-2080 streaming partial-response telemetry (ops).
- Slack thread #hosted-api-debugging for early design thoughts.

Appendix: example capture (truncated):
{
  "microturn_id": "mt-20250210-7a3",
  "frames": [
    {"seq": 1, "partial_text_delta": "User: How do I reset my password?"},
    {"seq": 2, "partial_text_delta": "Assistant: Sure — here's a short flow..."},
    {"seq": 3, "tool_event": {"type":"http","id":"t-9","request":"POST /auth/reset","start_ts":"...","end_ts":"...","outcome":"200"}},
    {"seq": 4, "partial_text_delta": "Assistant: I've sent a link to your email."},
    {"seq": 5, "final_structured_output": {"action":"send_email","email":"***REDACTED***"}, "schema_hash":"sha256:abc..."}
  ]
}

Contact: Maya Chen (product) — for prioritization and review.

Status: draft — looking for engineering spike + SRE cost estimate before moving to in_review.
